title: Watch the Nebuta floats go through Aomori
description: Illuminated paper warriors four metres tall, hauled through the streets for six nights each August by teams who shout and dance beside them.

title: Eat wanko soba until you cover the bowl
description: A server refills your bowl the moment you empty it, and keeps going until you slam the lid on. Fifteen bowls is one serving; a hundred is a story.

title: See the snow monsters on Zao
description: Fir trees encased in rime by wind off Siberia until they look like hunched figures. A ropeway runs up through them and they are lit at night.

title: Stay overnight at Ginzan Onsen in the snow
description: A gas-lit street of wooden ryokan either side of a river, in a valley that was a silver mine until 1689. Day visitors are limited in winter.

title: Watch the first sunrise of the year at Inubosaki
description: The first point on the main island to see the sun each morning, with an 1874 British-built lighthouse on the headland.

title: Walk the Jogasaki coastal path on Izu
description: Nine kilometres along a lava shoreline from a four-thousand-year-old eruption, crossed by two suspension bridges over the sea.

title: Cycle around the Fuji Five Lakes
description: Fifty kilometres linking five lakes formed when lava dammed the valleys, with the mountain in view for most of it.

title: Drive the Noto peninsula coast road
description: Rice terraces running down to the Sea of Japan, salt made by hand on the shore, and a beach firm enough to drive on at Chirihama.

title: See the thatched houses at Gokayama
description: The quieter half of the world heritage listing it shares with Shirakawa-go, with two small villages and a fraction of the coaches.

title: Bathe at Gero Onsen
description: Ranked one of the three great hot springs of Japan since the seventeenth century. A single pass gets you into three baths of your choosing.

title: See the cherry blossom on Mount Yoshino
description: Thirty thousand cherry trees planted up the mountainside in four bands that flower in sequence over about two weeks.

title: Ride the ropeway over Kobe at night
description: Ten minutes up over the city to a garden on the ridge, with the harbour laid out below and the Akashi bridge lit beyond it.

title: Take a boat through the Kurashiki canal quarter
description: White-walled rice warehouses along a willow-lined canal, kept because the town was too unimportant to bomb.

title: Climb to Nageiredo, the temple in the cliff
description: A national treasure wedged into a cliff face, reached by a climb up roots and chains that is closed in bad weather and requires proper shoes.

title: Watch the sun set over Lake Shinji
description: A brackish lake famous for its sunsets, with a small pine island that every photograph of Matsue seems to use.

title: Cycle the Shimanami Kaido across the islands
description: Seventy kilometres over six islands on dedicated cycleways slung under the road bridges, from Honshu to Shikoku.

title: Walk the Ritsurin garden at Takamatsu
description: Six ponds and thirteen landscaped hills laid out over a century from 1625, with Mount Shiun borrowed as the backdrop.

title: Be poled through the canals at Yanagawa
description: Four hundred and seventy kilometres of moat and canal from the old castle town, punted in flat boats with a brazier under the blanket in winter.

title: Walk Yufuin under Mount Yufu
description: A hot spring town of small galleries and a lake that steams on cold mornings, an hour inland from the crowds at Beppu.

title: Look for dolphins off Amakusa
description: A resident pod of around two hundred bottlenose dolphins in the Amakusa Sea, seen on most trips year round rather than seasonally.

title: Watch Sakurajima from the Kagoshima ferry
description: One of the most active volcanoes on earth, erupting most weeks, fifteen minutes across the bay on a ferry that runs all night.

title: Bathe in the Sakinoyu rock pool at Shirahama
description: An open-air bath cut into the rocks at the waterline, in use for over a thousand years, where waves break over the wall in a swell.

title: See the black keep at Matsumoto Castle
description: One of only twelve original keeps left standing in Japan, and the oldest of them, with steep timber stairs to the sixth floor.

title: Cycle between the palaces of Potsdam
description: Frederick the Great's summer palace on terraced vineyards, in a park of nearly three square kilometres with several more palaces in it.

title: Walk the Riesling terraces above the Rhine
description: Some of the steepest vineyards in Germany, worked by hand, with a monastery at Eberbach that has been making wine since 1136.

title: Ride the steam railway up the Brocken
description: A narrow-gauge steam line to 1,141 metres, on a summit that was a Cold War listening post and is in cloud two days out of three.

title: Walk the Garden Kingdom of Dessau-Worlitz
description: The first English landscape garden on the continent, 142 square kilometres of designed countryside from the 1760s, crossed by gondola.

title: Walk the Danish-German border at Flensburg
description: A harbour town that has been Danish and German by turns, where both languages are official and the rum trade left its warehouses behind.

title: Walk the Santander bay promenade to El Sardinero
description: Six kilometres of seafront from the ferry port to a Belle Epoque beach the Spanish royal family used to summer at.

title: Walk the walled old town of Caceres
description: Thirty towers and almost no modern buildings inside the walls, which is why film crews keep using it. Storks nest on most of the towers.

title: Walk the dinosaur footprints of the Rioja hills
description: Over ten thousand tracks in the sandstone of the Cameros basin, left in mud 120 million years ago and now tilted up on end.

title: Cycle the Turia riverbed park
description: The river was diverted after the 1957 flood and the old bed turned into nine kilometres of park through the middle of the city.

title: Go into the Frasassi caves
description: A chamber big enough to hold Milan cathedral, found by cavers in 1971, with a walkway through 1.5km of it.

title: Walk the Piano Grande when it flowers
description: A high plain that turns to sheets of poppy, cornflower and lentil flower for a few weeks each summer, below a village still rebuilding after 2016.

title: Walk the Somme battlefields and the Thiepval memorial
description: Seventy-two thousand names of men with no known grave, on a memorial that can be seen from most of the battlefield it stands over.

title: Ride the mechanical elephant at Nantes
description: A twelve-metre articulated elephant carrying fifty passengers around a former shipyard, built by a company that makes nothing else.

title: Ski Parnassos above Delphi
description: Greece's main ski area at 2,250 metres, an hour from Delphi, where on a clear day you can see the Gulf of Corinth from the lifts.

title: Swim at Damouchari on the Pelion coast
description: A pebble cove with no road down to it, reached on foot through olive terraces, on the peninsula the centaurs were supposed to live on.

title: Cycle the Confederation Trail across PEI
description: Four hundred and thirty-five kilometres tip to tip on the old railway, never steeper than two per cent because the trains could not manage it.

title: Watch beluga whales in the Churchill River
description: Around four thousand belugas come into the estuary each summer, curious enough to swim under a kayak and hum at you through the hull.

title: Stand under the monarch butterflies at El Rosario
description: Hundreds of millions of monarchs cluster on oyamel firs after flying from Canada. The sound of the wings is the part nobody expects.

title: Walk to the Texolo waterfall near Xico
description: An eighty-metre fall in a coffee-growing valley, crossed by an iron bridge that has appeared in more films than the town has hotels.

title: Walk the Wanuskewin bison trails
description: Six thousand years of Northern Plains habitation on one site, with bison returned to the land in 2019 and a medicine wheel above the valley.

title: Walk the Basaseachic falls in the Sierra Tarahumara
description: The second highest waterfall in Mexico at 246 metres, in Raramuri country where the running tradition comes from.

title: Walk on the sea floor at Hopewell Rocks
description: The highest tides in the world, up to sixteen metres. You walk among the stacks at low water and could kayak over them six hours later.

title: Swim off the free public beach at Tulum
description: The paid beach clubs sit either side of a stretch that is still public and free, with the same white sand and the ruins on the headland behind.

title: Walk the malecon at Cozumel in the evening
description: The cruise ships leave by six and the seafront goes back to being a town, with a plaza band on Sunday nights.

title: Watch sunrise over the Dieng plateau
description: A volcanic caldera at 2,000 metres with eighth-century Hindu temples, coloured sulphur lakes and frost on the potato fields in August.

title: Walk the Dutch colonial quarter of Semarang
description: A restored old town of Dutch East Indies warehouses and a 1753 church, on ground that is slowly sinking into the coast.

title: Stay in the cone houses at Wae Rebo
description: Seven conical thatched houses at 1,100 metres, reached by a three-hour walk in. You sleep in the communal house and the village performs the welcome ceremony on arrival.

title: Row through the karst at Rammang-Rammang
description: One of the largest limestone karst fields in the world, poled through on a wooden boat between towers of rock and rice paddies, an hour north of Makassar.

title: Look into the Sianok canyon at Bukittinggi
description: A hundred-metre fault valley on the equator, in Minangkabau country where property passes down the female line.

title: See the baroque churches of Old Goa
description: The capital of Portuguese India until cholera emptied it, leaving cathedrals in a village. St Francis Xavier's body is still on display in one.

title: Walk the kora around the Dalai Lama's temple
description: A circuit of the Tsuglagkhang complex, walked clockwise past prayer wheels by the Tibetan community that has lived here since 1960.

title: Take the ferry to Elephanta Island
description: Rock-cut Shiva temples from the fifth century on an island an hour off the Gateway of India, with a six-metre three-headed Sadashiva at the centre.

title: See the temple carvings at Khajuraho
description: Twenty-five surviving temples of an original eighty-five, covered in sculpture of which only a small fraction is the erotic work they are known for.

title: Walk the cleanest village in Asia
description: A Khasi village that took the title in 2003 and kept it, with bamboo bins on every path and a community rota that still runs.
